Every example is a BoxLang script that makes a complete piece of sound from code, with no samples and no licensing questions: all the music is original. The clips below are short renders at 96 kbps; the scripts make the full pieces. Each is one readable file in [`examples/`](https://github.com/ortus-boxlang/bx-audio/tree/development/examples), covered by tests that render it and measure what it sounds like.

```bash
bx-audio pieces                         # the list
bx-audio render house --out=house.mp3   # render one, with its own settings
bx-audio explorer                       # play them all in the browser
```

## Pop Drive

*Upbeat pop.* Voices, a beat grid, kick pump and mastering. A port of a numpy script, checked against the original.

<audio controls preload="none" src="../assets/audio/pop-drive.mp3"></audio>

```bash
bx-audio render pop-drive --out=pop-drive.mp3
```

| Setting | | Range | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--bars` | Bars | 8 to 56 | `28` |
| `--bpm` | Tempo | 90 to 150 | `128` |
| `--style` | Style | pop, drive | `pop` |

[Script and notes](https://github.com/ortus-boxlang/bx-audio/tree/development/examples/01-pop-drive)

## Chiptune

*8 bit game music.* Original music for an imaginary console: two pulse channels, a triangle bass and noise drums. Five tracks, from an overworld theme to a boss fight.

<audio controls preload="none" src="../assets/audio/chiptune.mp3"></audio>

```bash
bx-audio render chiptune --out=chiptune.mp3
```

| Setting | | Range | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--track` | Track | overworld, cave, boss, title, victory | `overworld` |
| `--loops` | Loops (0 is the track's own) | 0 to 4 | `0` |

[Script and notes](https://github.com/ortus-boxlang/bx-audio/tree/development/examples/08-chiptune)

## Game sound effects

*Sound effects.* A jump, a coin, a laser, an explosion and more, made from pulse waves and noise. Hear them all in the sampler or one at a time.

<audio controls preload="none" src="../assets/audio/sfx.mp3"></audio>

```bash
bx-audio render sfx --out=sfx.mp3
```

| Setting | | Range | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--sound` | Sound | sampler, jump, coin, laser, explosion, powerup, hit, blip, alarm, gameover, footstep | `sampler` |
| `--seed` | Seed (the noise in the explosion, hit and footstep) | 1 to 99 | `1` |

[Script and notes](https://github.com/ortus-boxlang/bx-audio/tree/development/examples/09-sfx)

## Voice-over

*Narration over music.* A trailer style announcement: a text to speech voice over music that ducks under it. Needs the speech engine, so it runs from the command line.

<audio controls preload="none" src="../assets/audio/voiceover.mp3"></audio>

```bash
bx-audio render voiceover --out=voiceover.mp3
```

| Setting | | Range | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--voice` | Voice | text | `kristin` |
| `--speed` | Speaking speed | 0.7 to 1.3 | `0.96` |
| `--text` | Lines, separated by \| | text | `none` |
| `--duck` | Music ducking in dB | -24 to 0 | `-12` |
| `--bpm` | Tempo | 80 to 130 | `100` |

[Script and notes](https://github.com/ortus-boxlang/bx-audio/tree/development/examples/12-voiceover)

## Trailer soundtrack

*A scored video.* Music cut to an exact length, a voice-over with captions, ducking, mastering to a loudness target and chapter markers. Needs the speech engine, so it runs from the command line.

<audio controls preload="none" src="../assets/audio/trailer.mp3"></audio>

```bash
bx-audio render trailer --out=trailer.mp3
```

| Setting | | Range | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--seconds` | Length in seconds | 8 to 40 | `15` |
| `--voice` | Voice | text | `kristin` |
| `--speed` | Speaking speed | 0.7 to 1.3 | `0.96` |
| `--text` | What the voice says | text | `none` |
| `--target` | Loudness target | streaming, podcast, game, broadcast, cinema | `streaming` |

[Script and notes](https://github.com/ortus-boxlang/bx-audio/tree/development/examples/13-trailer)

## Game audio

*A scripted play session.* What a game asks of a sound engine: effects with variations, a looping theme, a boss theme made with time stretch and pitch shift, and a real time mixer with music and effects buses. A scripted session is rendered here.

<audio controls preload="none" src="../assets/audio/game-audio.mp3"></audio>

```bash
bx-audio render game-audio --out=game-audio.mp3
```

| Setting | | Range | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--seed` | Seed (changes the variations) | 1 to 20 | `1` |

[Script and notes](https://github.com/ortus-boxlang/bx-audio/tree/development/examples/14-game-audio)
